content: If you have not taken this medication for more than 14 days, you may begin taking the extended-release tablets immediately. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. If you stop taking this medication for more than 7 days for reasons other than the serious reactions described in the Warning section, consult your doctor for instructions on how to restart treatment. It is crucial to continue taking this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not skip any doses. Do not increase your dose, take this drug more frequently than prescribed, or stop taking it (or other HIV medications) even for a short time unless directed by your doctor. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Common side effects may include tiredness, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Rarely, drowsiness may occur. You may notice the empty extended-release tablet shell in your stool. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to combat infections you already had, potentially causing disease symptoms to reappear. Additionally, you may experience symptoms if your immune system becomes overactive. This reaction can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or many months later. Nevirapine commonly causes a rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe reaction. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare, but seek immediate medical attention if they occur. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking nevirapine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may rarely cause drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can increase drowsiness. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV infection to your baby, and nevirapine may be part of that treatment. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications can affect the removal of nevirapine from your body, which may impact how nevirapine works. Examples include rifamycins (such as rifampin). Nevirapine can accelerate the removal of many other medications from your body, potentially affecting their effectiveness. Do not use prednisone to prevent a rash, as it can increase the risk of a rash during the first 6 weeks of nevirapine treatment. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods such as pills, patches, or rings, which could result in pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In case of overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as liver function, viral load, T-cell counts) should be conducted while you are taking this medication. Attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose. Take your next dose at the regular time. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in August 2024. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
